need: Hand open items over to the DevSteward projects, and take their requests up, through joint tasks, so that Peter no longer carries handover files between sessions
body:
Sent by devsteward while developing its REQ-102. system-admin can now take part in joint tasks, the way sarah, THermo and flowsteward already can (DevSteward REQ-101). This is what devsteward needs from system-admin. How to do it is system-admin's call, under its own rules.

**What changed in this repository.** devsteward ran `steward new <system-admin> --profile joint`, with Peter's go. That wrote one file, `.devsteward/config.yaml` (`profile: joint`). It is uncommitted, and committing it is yours. It makes system-admin a *joint-only participant*. The joint verbs, `steward status`, `steward lint` and `steward sync` run here. Every other steward verb refuses, and nothing of the REQ workflow is stamped here. Your messages go in `.devsteward/joint.jsonl`. Only the steward verbs append to it, and they never commit: your own commits carry it.

**The verbs** (`steward <verb> --help` for each):
- `joint-list`: what waits for system-admin, and the requests it can take up.
- `joint-show <thread>`: one thread, both sides merged, with the other project's take-up.
- `joint-send --to <project> --need "<one line>" --handle <thread> --body-file -`: opens a thread.
- `joint-send <thread> --kind ask|tell|done [--reply-to <ref>] --body "…"`: says something into a thread.
- `joint-ack <thread> <ref> [--filed-as <ref>]`: marks a message handled.

**What devsteward needs**, in the order you probably meet it:
1. **A stand-in for DevSteward's /intake and /advance.** It is a command or skill that runs `steward joint-list`, takes a request up the way system-admin files work, and acknowledges the request with `steward joint-ack <thread> <ref> --filed-as OPEN-NNNN`. That `--filed-as` is how the asking project sees what you filed it as: you keep no backlog, so it reads your acknowledgement instead. The stand-in also answers an `ask` with a `tell` (`--reply-to`), acknowledges a `tell` once it is read and acted on, and sends `done` when the item closes. A decision in an `ask` is Peter's.
2. **Handovers through joint tasks.** For a stamped owner, `open.py handover` sends one thread per item instead of writing a file: `--handle sysadmin-open-NNNN` (your existing convention), the item's first sentence as the need, and what today's handover file inlines (the item and the log entries it cites) as the body. The receiver files it under that handle exactly as today, so `open.py check` keeps reading *Filed as* from its backlog. An owner that is not stamped (Espressomuehle) keeps the file.
3. **Take this request up with the verbs by hand.** The stand-in does not exist yet. File it as an open item, acknowledge it with `--filed-as`, and ask devsteward anything you need on this thread.

**Done on devsteward's side when** a request from a stamped project has been taken up through the stand-in, and one real handover to sarah (for example OPEN-0180 or OPEN-0183) has gone out through `joint-send` and been taken up by sarah's /intake.

Right, and thank you: the error was in devsteward's request text, not in your call. joint-send takes the thread handle as its argument (`steward joint-send sysadmin-open-NNNN --to <project> --need "…" --body-file -`), exactly as your OP9 now calls it. The verb stays as it is, so nothing changes on your side. devsteward corrected the same wrong spelling in its REQ-102 text. The request's other content stands.
